- ProgressTimeline to the full spec (and the reference recording's alignment): no two-step layout at any width; wide (usable = width - 2 x 128 holds two minimum segments) -> first dot 128 from the left, last 128 from the right, a middle step's dot at 40% of the width slid on to show the next whole, never past keeping the current readable, clamped; narrow -> the current dot at 50% in every state, first and last too, on a track padded by half the width each end; arrows scroll one actual segment per click (smooth, clamped, quick clicks add up, instant with reduced motion) instead of a show-all callback (onArrow / progress-timeline:arrow tell the host). Validation: 2,120 mounts plus drag, trackpad, touch, keyboard, arrow navigation, re-render, resize, reduced motion; 0 failures. Demo published: https://claude.ai/artifact/5GjkoiJnJsLCMLCsimt9f5
- Sub step timeline chevrons 24 (from 28), still on the line, with a 32px backdrop blur; their chevrons 12.
- Report visuals: the date badge in the mono ("Saans Mono", falling back to the system mono; named, never embedded) at 12px.
- Sub step timeline: no padding is ever added (it left a blank lead-in); a timeline that fits stretches to fill; narrow centring only as far as the track allows; an arrow shows only where its side overflows AND a connector runs under its centre (not over a dot or empty track). Steps' minimum width a tweak (Tweaks > Sub steps > Minimum width, 128 by default, 64-240), the track placed again as it moves.
- Retired tweaks: Sub timeline placement (in the status card kept), ETA badge (Off kept).
- Journey card with no heading (a locked page): no band above Complete first, desk and phone; the page's own (locked) title full white, the others (the one to complete first, the rest locked) white 40%.
- Stress test page rules list: minimum widths that stretch to fill, narrow centring without blank space, arrows only over the line, the Minimum width tweak named.
- Sub step timeline arrows: shown whenever their side fades and the timeline is under them (line, dot or a step's label column; never blank track past an end) -- the connector-only rule hid the left one beside a dot ("why is there no arrow left when there's a gradient and a step on the left"). While an arrow's own scroll runs, visibility is judged at where it lands, so a dot passing under doesn't blink it out and swallow the next click. Same rule in ProgressTimeline (and its narrow layout: no blank lead-in, columns stretch to fill when every one fits).
- ProgressTimeline, from the adversarial review (findings still true under the current spec): contain:inline-size so 1fr cells, flex:1 children and table cells don't grow to the track; width from layout (computed style / the observer's contentRect), not the transformed on-screen size; undefined options don't override defaults (edge: undefined stayed 0); small custom edges no longer shift the track (negative first-column margin, the track clipped on x); browsing = any scroll the component didn't start (so paused swipes, assistive tech, focus scrolls count, and a tap during the automatic scroll doesn't freeze it); an ordinary re-render leaves the scroll (and any arrow/key animation) alone; arrows and keys share one accumulating target, reset on a progress change; the mouse drag's release heard on the window (no ghost drag); focus falls back to the track, a visible arrow or the card, never <body>; forced-colours styles; arrowLabels option; the observer relays out on the next frame (no loop error); narrow fades give way so the centred label stays clear below 384px. Each has a regression test; 172,328 checks, 0 failures.
- Microbiome: the questionnaire's done page isn't a page ("this step doesn't exist"): any open of gutq done (the progress card's summary, a stale link) lands on the microbiome's step in hand (gut, its SIM state).
- Modal V9 (Tweaks > Sub steps > Modal): the service's report card from Report visuals as the modal -- Whole Body MRI -> mri, Microbiome -> gut, Advanced Blood -> blood, DEXA -> dexa (others, e.g. the plan, keep V1). report-visuals.html#solo-<card> shows that one card alone, transparent, with the presets set on the Report visuals page (same origin, same storage); it posts its height, its square's colour and place, its buttons' clicks and Escape; the host runs its own (hidden) buttons by their words, and its close is drawn as the card's 8px square. Desk: centred, 440 wide, the shadow on the card's shape; phone: a floating card, not the sheet.

## Timeline search behaves like the Insights search

"Same search behaviour as the Biomarker insight search, (with clear cross when typed) … with keyboard / styles / etc".

At every breakpoint:
- A grey-disc clear cross appears once something is typed. It clears the text without taking or giving focus.
- A keystroke runs the list through the Insights search's 380ms beat, with a skeleton built from the timeline's own row classes (`#dTl .tlSkel`, so it takes each breakpoint's layout). An empty query lands at once, and a page change mid-beat lands it immediately.
- Enter drops focus. Escape clears the field and drops focus, without reaching the page's own Escape handlers.

At XS:
- The open field is the Insights field: 56 tall, 14 radius, a 1.5 edge (white when focused, ink on paper), no fill, a 20px icon and 15px text. The title under it is hidden.
- The head row keeps the icon's 44px, so opening the field no longer shifts the page by 14px.
- The phone's drawn keyboard is cloned into `#bpFrame` and rises on focus (`body.tlKbd`). The dock leaves while it is up, and the list gets 300px of foot room.
- The keys type into the field. The search key drops the keyboard.
- A wheel or drag on the page drops the keyboard. A list changing height under it does not.
- The field closes back to its icon when it is let go empty.

## Auto on a narrow window is XS; the dock keeps the format; type tweaks

- **Auto below 600px is XS** ("auto on a small viewport should reflect the XS styles"; "XS just add a frame iPhone for the sake of the test").
  - Auto sets `data-bp="xs"` plus `html.bpAuto`. It lives on `<html>` because `setMode` rewrites `body.className`.
  - `html.bpAuto` drops the device: no bezel, no 48px insets or 56px corners, no drawn status strip or keys, and `--bpW` is 100vw. The dock stays at the foot, and the strip's top clearance stays so the page matches the framed XS.
  - The forced XS keeps its iPhone frame for testing.
  - Crossing 600px on resize re-runs the select's change, so pages redraw.
  - `resize()` adds the 48px only when a device is drawn.
- **Window-size switching**: the Overview family left `RESP_FAMILIES`, so a narrow window keeps the desk Overview, Timeline and service pages at XS instead of the old Mobile page (v6). Insights has no XS desk, so it keeps its phone (v20). `responsiveSync` runs only in Auto.
- **The docks keep the format** ("Auto → new page Auto, XS → new page XS").
  - In XS (forced or Auto), Overview, Timeline and Services open the desk pages in the same breakpoint, from either dock.
  - Insights opens its phone page: full screen in Auto's window, in its shell beside the forced frame.
  - The breakpoint select is never changed by navigation.
  - `#bpFrame` hides on phone pages (`m5`, `m6`) so no empty device sits over them.

## Review fixes (workflow review of the My journey V2 changes; 4 confirmed)
- Later reached from elsewhere (the Overview's More services → `_tl.tab('claim')`) while the bento or the year hides the tabs left no way back to Upcoming. render() now marks `#dTl.tlClaim` while Later shows, and the bento/year only hide the bar/tabs `:not(.tlClaim)`, so the tabs come back over Later; Upcoming brings the bento back.
- The year's head jumped to the year's end when the list had nothing to scroll (a tall window) and didn't move after a search: jtAt returns the first milestone's start when the scroll is 0-long; filter() redraws the head (JTU).
- Add to plan left the colonoscopy among Timeline v1's section suggestions (shown twice): v1's sec() now drops answered suggestions too (`askGone()`, shared with the milestones').
- The bento kept "In your plan" after the added colonoscopy was put off from its page: the added row is kept (`a.added`); put off, its gap opens again as "Saved for later" and the count goes back up.

## Locked phases with reasons, group visual, timeline terms

- **Timeline terms:** the phases are **Baseline** (0–3 months · Understand your health), **Act & Improve** (4–9 months · Follow your personalised plan) and **Re-test & Refine** (9–12 months · Measure progress and adjust). The descriptors replace the months on the tabs, the rail, the phase header and the card variant; the year card keeps its month labels (its columns are narrow). The transitions read "Act & Improve" and "Re-test & Refine".
- **Locked phase card:** no "Shaped by your baseline". It says why the phase comes next (a lead line and three reasons, each a small card: Act & Improve — made for your results, deeper tests as needed, guided by your doctor; Re-test & Refine — see what changed, adjust your plan, your next year). ### Blood stream, rebuilt in 3D; Amount
- "The blood stream needs to feel much more three-dimensional, spacious and fluid ... a large invisible curved vessel moving through 3D space ... depth, perspective, scale variation and negative space ... orange particles attached to positions in the vessel, flowing with it, most outside the viewport, entering progressively ... slow continuous 3D motion ... lighter ... the viewport a camera on a much larger world": its own layer now (streamLayer). A vessel 14 units long around a camera that travels beside it; its middle line sweeping in height (1.3 + .55) and depth (2 + .6); radius .95. Inside it seven strands twisting along it (each its distance from the middle, place round it, twist and width) carrying most of the points, and a sparse faint fill. Every point flows along the vessel a little faster than the camera travels (.26 vs .13 units a second), so the stream drifts left to right past the view and wraps out of sight at either end. True perspective (focal 1.05x the screen's height): nearer larger (to 4.2px) and brighter, fading very near and far off. The camera follows the vessel loosely (so it wanders through the frame, nearing and receding), its height and depth drifting and rolling a few degrees.
- The hero's labels: 26 orange points fixed in the vessel (spread along all of it, at their own place round its middle), flowing with it, so a few are in view at a time and others come in as it brings them; each label opens on one in the box that will stay there while it is read (checked 5.6s ahead), the next words from the bag; none in reach, it waits for the vessel to bring one. 30fps, ~40-45fps measured.
- "Create also a tweak: amount of particles, 0 to 100, in addition to condense": Amount (0-100, 50 by default): .25x to 1.75x the points, both balls and the stream. Condense and Amount now show for Sphere and Sphere hero. Condense on the stream: how many points ride the strands and how tight they are.
- "Active marker position must be on this area" (Sphere hero, and the Blood stream's labels): the active label's square now lands in the ball's middle: from 23% in to the middle of the width (the words have room to its right), 250 to 114 above the button (the 64 safe space kept). The ball turns as far as it takes to bring one there; the stream waits for one to flow in.
- "Tweak What this means for you: accent card, default text (not Key takeaway); keep Copy for both": Meaning (Accent card default / Default text). Default text: the takeaway's paragraphs as the section's own (no card, no bulb, no Key takeaway), Copy a pill at the section's top right, level with its heading; Copy copies the same words in both.
- Rest of this round: the active label's area (Sphere hero, Blood stream) narrowed to the ball's middle.
- "active always above everything": the open label sits over every other label's square (z-index 3 while open, dropped once it has folded back).

## The Health profile on its own (dist/health-profile.html, https://claude.ai/artifact/27KVVvtwN5n6VRit7JSrUZ)

- "Create an independent artifact that only includes the Health profile flow; all changes on this artifact should impact the other."
- **How it stays in step**: `tools/build-hp.js` makes it from `index.html` on every build (`tools/build.js` calls it at the end). It takes, by content rather than line numbers:
  - the report sheet's `<style>` (the `--ar-` tokens),
  - the Health profile's `<style>` (`.arSheet.hpSheet`),
  - the Health profile's `<script>` (`window.HealthProfile`).
  So any change to the flow in the prototype is in the next build of both. **Every publish now republishes both artifacts.**
- **The page**:
  - The sheet full screen from its intro (on a wide screen a column up to 1040 with rounded corners, the desk rail inside), in the viewer's theme.
  - A small **Demo** menu: theme (Dark/Light), state (Step 1 … Done, with the dropped-off states) and Start over. On a phone it's a pill under the sheet's button, opening upward; on a wide screen a round button in the gutter.
  - X at the intro just stays on the intro (there's no page under it). Escape behaves as in the prototype.
- No fonts or images are embedded (system fonts, as the prototype). It's about 240 KB, unminified.
- **Standalone: the Viewport, as the prototype's** ("I need the XS breakpoint tweak here, same as the other artifact"): Demo → Viewport, Auto / XS / S / M / L.
  - XS: the reference phone, 393 wide, 56 corners, the black bezel in its steel rim. Its status bar (time, island, signal) is taken from the prototype's own `#bpFrame` markup at build time and drawn over the sheet, white on dark and black on light. The sheet's bar sits 58 down, as in the prototype's device.
  - S: the tablet, 600 wide, 28 corners, a wider bezel, its small status strip, bar 44 down.
  - M 992 and L 1440: unframed, the desk layout with the rail.
  - Auto: the window (a column up to 1040 on a wide one).
  - It starts on XS where the phone fits (a phone itself starts on Auto), and the last pick is remembered. The Demo button sits 28 right of the device when there's room, else the pill under the sheet's button.

## Health profile welcome: dot to sphere, written title, hugging CTA

- The first-time welcome now opens on a single dot in the middle of the sheet. It is drawn in at 0.15 s, breathes, and at 0.65 s bursts into the sphere (1.1 s: each point flung out a little after the one before, slightly past its place and back, a faint ring going out ahead). The feeding motes join once the ball has formed. `sphere({ burst: true })` holds the ball until `burst(at, lead)` is called; every other sphere is unchanged.

Across the last line the letters get quicker and cooler, the last word 1.15 s at 70%. ## The blink and the clipping: the welcome's paper fading on its own

- **Found on video**, not in the canvas: the welcome sheet carries the sheet's own `transition: background-color .4s`. Making it see-through for the hand-off therefore faded its paper out over 0.4 s.
  - **Going forward**, the sphere was already under it in the profile, so it vanished for 4–5 frames and came back: the blink. The profile's page, rising underneath, also stayed hidden and popped in at the end.
  - **Going back**, the welcome mounted over the profile hid the profile's page and halo straight away and showed them again: the clipping.
- **The fix:** the welcome is made see-through at once, `transition: none` alongside the transparent background, in both directions. After Back, it gets its paper back at once and its own transition again.
- **Back now goes down** ("this should transition down, and the intro content should appear from top to down"), as the profile goes back from a step to its intro:
  - the profile's page (halo with it), its button and bar go down 72 and fade (0.38 s, accelerating);
  - the welcome's words and button come down from a third of the screen above (0.66 s from 0.3 s, easing out);
  - the sphere drops to its place and grows to its 110% in step (0.9 s);
  - in the bottom-sheet format, the frame is drawn in to the sheet (0.62 s from 0.2 s).
  - This replaces the time-reversed playback, whose reversed easing kept both pages nearly still and then snapped them away at the end.
- **Checked:** the sphere's screen position and size every frame (no jump, nothing scrolling or overflowing beside it); 25 fps video of Get started and Back (the sphere visible throughout); and frozen frames at 0–1050 ms in both directions.

## Overview: the primary card's section back; one card colour. Welcome card: halo, padding, age, texture

- **Primary card gone on XS: found.** Dragging any section card in Tweaks rewrote `stOvOrder` with the groups' keys. The Primary card group's key `primary` is not a section name, so `order()` dropped it. When the profile card is the primary card it sits in the top row, but that row moved as part of Next step (`hero`), which then came near the end. So the whole top row went to the foot of the page and Services rose to the top.
  - `order()` now reads `primary` as the Primary card's section (`prof`, or `hero` once Dexa next).
  - `gEnd` writes that section name.
  - With the profile card in the top row, `applyD` moves the row as the profile's unit.
  - The profile's section stands at the first of Next step / profile in the order. It is first by default and can now be dragged under Services or elsewhere.
- **One card colour on the Overview:** the primary card's, #fff 4% on dark and #2e1f1a 6% on light, hovered at 8% / 9%.
  - Before: insights were 6% / cream #fdfaf3, Later a solid #1d1d1d / #f4f4f3, the Action plan cards an outline with no fill, Coverage & age 5.5%, the booked card 4%.
  - `--ovCard` / `--ovCardH` on `#dOver`.
  - Next step keeps its dark brown and the Program card its dark. The Tab layout's folder keeps its colours.
- **Welcome card:**
  - The halo is a 0.5 px border only. The blurred light around it is gone.
  - Padding is 8 more all round (32 at the sides, 26–30 top and bottom), front and back. On the back, the member number's column takes its full width, so it is no longer cut.
  - The age is back in the normal font, 12 px, full ink (white on dark), 10 px under the name (was 12).
- **Card texture** (Tweaks → Welcome → Texture: Dots / Rings / Halftone / Off; Strength 0–100, default 40 for "less visible by 60%"; Spacing 2–8 px, default 3; Motion on/off).
  - A canvas on the card's face (`w2Tex`), drawn in the card's ink in the bottom-right corner, with a radial CSS mask that fades it toward the middle.
  - Dots: a fine 1 px grid. A band of light sweeps out from the corner for 2.6 s every 7 s, and the odd dot glints.
  - Rings: 0.5 px quarter circles about the corner, with a pulse running out through them.
  - Halftone: dots growing toward the corner, breathing slowly.
  - The sweep runs fast leaving the corner, slow through the middle, and fast again (u + .75·sin 2πu / 2π).

## Welcome V2: the dot's pull, the lines at the foot, a burst; name and age closer

- "The rotating lines should be at the bottom of the screen; the dot in the middle with particles attracting inside, floating around; the more I progress, the more particles; at some point the dot becomes small and explodes."
  - The status lines sit at the foot of the screen, 132 px off the bottom (92 in the desk's modal), where the buttons will come. They were under the dot.
  - `w2Att`, a canvas over the dark: specks (white, a third of them the warm light) come in from round the dot, 70 px out to 40% of the screen. They drift in turning (pull 110 + 8800/d px/s², drag), fade in, dim as they near the dot and are swallowed there.
  - The rate steps up with each line: 8, 16, then 28 a second.
  - At the end the dot is drawn in to a point (`--hpDR` to 1.2 px, 420 ms, ease-in). Then it bursts: the opening (Full screen spread or Card shape morph) starts and the specks are flung out (260–780 px/s), fading over 0.9 s.

## The "drop shadow" in the card; padding 8 less; the age 14 px

- "It feels like there's a drop shadow in the card." Measured down a column across the card's top edge, with the user's settings (Filled, Fill blur 0, Mask on, Blanket 0): 199 → 194 → 186 above it, then 181 → 175 → 168 inside. That is a smooth fall, and it does not change with the face's highlight, the blur, the halo, the texture, the motes or the blanket switched off (only removing the fill or the highlight changes it, darker by 1 to 5). It is the background's own light falling off from gold to brown right at the card's top edge, most of all with Title below, where the light was raised to sit above the card. So it reads as a shadow the card casts.
- **Light position** (Tweaks → First-time user, −160 to +160 px, default 0) moves the picture, and the loading light with it, up or down behind the card (`--hpW2BgY`). About +64 puts the card in the light and the shadow is gone.
- The card's padding is 8 less all round, front and back: the logo at 24/18, the badge at 22/20, the name and age at 24 from the left and 22 from the foot; on the back, 24/22.
- The age is 14 px (was 12), still 6 px under the name.

## Welcome V2: the footer's gap; the light in code

- "Is the orange background an image or code? I would like to have control on it." It was the given picture, with a CSS gradient under it only as its fallback. It can now be drawn in code: **Light source** (Image / Code, Image the default).
  - Code is a glow centred 42% down the picture's height, as the picture's own, over a dim sky going into the dark.
  - Its colours are **Light** (the glow's core, #ffd99d), **Warm** (round it, #e9983e) and **Deep** (#6d2305), each a swatch with its hex. **Spread** (20–90%, default 46) sets how tall the glow is.

## Protocol card: a big Everlab mark in glossy ink

- "On the Protocol card, a big Everlab logo mark that bleeds over the card, like a glossy ink we usually see on a business card."
  - **Logo mark** (Off / Glossy) is a card setting, saved in each membership's preset: Protocol's default is Glossy, the others Off.
  - The Everlab mark is drawn half again the card's height (150%), bleeding off its bottom right (right −15%, bottom −34%), under the words, the face clipping it. It is the mark's SVG as a mask (data URI) on a filled element.
  - The fill is tone on tone, a lacquer: on a solid card its own colour a shade into its ink, lighter at the top, deeper at the foot. A white glint sweeps across it every 7 s, standing still with reduced motion.
  - On glass and the other styles it is drawn in the card's ink at 10%.

## Light palettes, scale, a longer light, Filled's text colour, particles

- "I don't want 3 colours, I want you to propose a few options." Code's three colour pickers are replaced by a **Palette** of five, each a chip of its glow (the one in use ringed, its name beside them): **Sunrise** (the picture's own: #ffd99d / #e9983e / #6d2305), **Ember** (deeper, redder), **Honey** (golden), **Copper** (muted), **Dusk** (rose to plum). Their state is a hidden select, kept with the Tweaks. Spread stays.
- "Need a controller to scale the bg": **Scale** (60–200%, default 100) sizes the light, the picture or the code, from its top (`scale` on `.hpW2Img`, the loading light with it).
- "The bg should go a bit more below the card": the picture's box is now 76% of the screen tall (was 64), the picture its same size (`background-size` 109.5%; light mode 176.8%). Its light carries on fading for about 120 px under the card (to 648 of 853 on the phone; it ended at the card's foot). The code's glow is kept where it was in the taller box.
- "On card Filled I also need a foreground controller": the card's **Text** colour row shows with Filled as well as Solid and colours its words, logo, badge and texture.
- The palette chips' ring was flattened by the panel's own button reset; it is now forced.
- "A controller to add more dense particles around the card": **Particles** (0–400%, default 100) sets how many warm specks float in to the card: 64 at 100%, live (`w2Motes().count`).

- **The grey during the burst (the user's recording):** the grain sat over the whole screen with `mix-blend-mode: overlay`. While the opening's radial mask was on, the light's layer was its own group, so the grain blended with nothing under the light and showed as a flat grey slab over the bottom of the screen until the mask lifted. The grain now lives in the picture itself (`.hpW2Bg > .hpW2Img::after`, its size divided by the light's Scale), blending with the picture alone. The bottom stays the sheet's dark all through.

It is now masked to the dot's own size (`--hpW2Ri`, registered) at the dot's place (`--hpW2Oy`, animated on it too). It rises with the light, then grows a little and fades (0.52 s) as the light bursts out of it.

At 4.25 s it condenses into the dot: it scales to a flat line, then to a point, blurring (0.75 s). Letter spacing is left alone so its lines never re-wrap and jump. The dot comes at 4.65 s and the lines start at 5.7 s. Images entrance: the second title rises away at 4.25 s and the photos start at 4.6 s.

The stage is two rows, so the desk formulas use 2 rows: modal H + 342 + 2 rows, Dy = (2 rows − 90) / 2. Title below: H + 358 + 2 rows. The phone stage's foot is a row higher, so the titles stay put.

## Flip glass at XS / S; the card logo's cycle

- Card flip at XS and S ("card bg clip on flip; Auto works well; XS clips"): reproduced with a frozen clock. Under the phone's (and the tablet's) rounded screen clip (the Health profile wrapper, overflow hidden with a 56 / 28 px radius), the browser ignores the glass's outline cut and draws the turning card's glass as a flat rectangle round it. ## Comments on the prototype; Step 0 after checkout; Records card coloured; Book a time

- **Comments** ("a comment system that actually works depending on the view / tweak selected"):
  - **Comments** in the bar, beside Refresh, with this view's open count on it. Pressing it turns comment mode on: the panel at the right, and the pins.
  - **Leaving one**: click anywhere on the prototype to leave a comment there. It pins to the element clicked, at the point clicked, and follows it as the page scrolls or moves.
  - **What it saves**: the view it was made on, meaning the version, the page or overlay over it (the Health profile, its reveal, a Documentation tab…), the viewport, the mode, and every tweak that page shows (the Tweaks rows not hidden for it, and the bar's own selects).
  - **When it shows**: its pin only when all of that matches again. Change a tweak it was made with and the pin goes; set it back and it returns.
  - **The panel**: This view and All. A comment from another view says what differs (e.g. "Primary card → State: Step 1 (now Step 3)") and has **Go to view**, which sets its version, page, viewport, mode and tweaks back, then opens its thread.
  - **A thread**: replies, Resolve / Reopen, and Delete (pressed twice). Resolved ones are hidden unless Show resolved is on. Your name is asked once.
  - **Storage**: kept in this browser, and followed across this page's tabs. **Copy all** and **Import** carry them to someone else's browser. A shared store across viewers would need a capability this account doesn't have.
  - Escape closes a thread, then the mode. With comments off, the prototype is untouched.

## Comments shared with everyone; @tags; Go to view switches fully; Records card colour

- **Comments are shared** ("visible by everyone and autosaved for everyone"):
  - Inside claude.ai the page uses the artifact's shared store (`db`). Every comment, reply, resolve and delete is saved as it happens, for everyone in the organisation who opens the page, and appears live in every open view.
  - Authors are the people viewing (`user`), kept by their id and named as each viewer sees them.
  - Opened outside claude.ai, comments stay in that browser as before (the panel says "This browser" or "Shared").
  - Comments made in this browser before sharing existed get a "Share N comments kept in this browser" button.
  - Anyone can resolve or reply. Delete is for the author (or the artifact's owner).
  - Comments are numbered in the order they were made.
  - Declared: `{ downloads, db, user: { scopes: ["profile"] } }`. A page with `db` stays inside the organisation (it already was).
- **@tags** ("need to be able to tag someone"):
  - Type @ and a name. Shared: the organisation's people, searched as you type, kept by their id. In this browser: the names seen here, or a new one tagged as typed.
  - Arrows and Enter/Tab pick, or click. A tag shows highlighted; **Mentions** lists the comments that tag you.
  - Tags notify nobody: there is no notification channel.
- **Buttons**: Comment beside Cancel and Reply at the right, the same height. The page's own `.cmGo` style had been pulling them out of place; every comment class is now `evc…`.
- **Go to its view switches fully** ("really need to swap fully to the other view"):

- **Changing page closes the Health profile** ("move to page sometimes keeps the XS view"): picking any version but Health profile or Membership reveal closes it and its reveal.

It shows "Uploading…" with a thin bar filling for about a second, then its date, kind and size, e.g. "March 2025 · PDF · 284 KB". There's no file picker any more.
- **The list** ("need to see the list of reports added"): the reports sit under the upload row in its card, one per line, the name in one line and the details below.
- **Bin with hesitation** ("need a bin icon, with hesitation: are you sure, yes / no, inline"): each report has a bin. Pressing it shows "Remove?" No / Yes in its place, focus on No. No puts the bin back; Yes folds the line away and drops the report. Only one asks at a time.
- **Line under the title**:
  - "You can also add them later" while there are none.
  - "1 document added", "2 documents added"… once there are some ("X document added if any added").
- **Two cards** ("2 cards instead, gap 8px; remove icon left to save space"):
  - Each row is its own grey secondary card, 8px apart, with no icon tile at the left; the reports list has no icons either.
  - Card corners 22px, the Overview primary card's ("card style same as overview primary card in radius and padding"), and 24px inside ("padding 24px"). The primary card's own padding is 20px (28px on the wide Overview).
- **Upload** button 44px high ("44px height"). The Yes / No buttons are 32px.
- **Tell me when they're ready is a switch** ("toggle"): grey track and light knob when off; white track with the knob across when on. Saved as before.
- Checked:
  - Switch on, saved.
  - Two uploads: Uploading… then their details.
  - Bin → Remove? No / Yes; No keeps it; Yes removes it, and the store keeps the other.
  - Lines 1 / 2 documents added; Upload 44px; radius 22, padding 24.
  - No errors.
- **Fixed: the profile's top light as a block at the left on desktop** ("bug bg here, should be the visual only on top"). The light carried over from the reveal was placed in pixels when the profile opened. Switching the breakpoint (XS → L) or widening the window with the profile open left it at the phone's 393px at the left. It is now placed as shares of the frame (left, top, width, height in %, its lift in % of its own height), so it follows the frame. Opened straight on desktop it sits exactly as before (1440 × 769, lifted 389px). XS → L with it open now spans the top.

A 5px solid square sits on each corner. Tweak inside Past results: **Frame trails** (0 to 100%, 35%). Checked: the settled box round the east coast with its corner squares and three towns lit; faint trails; no errors.

- **Each map style saved on its own** ("want to be able to save the map style independently; need a save button"): under Map style, a Style settings row with **Save Crosshair** / **Save Frame** (it names the style showing) and its state (Saved / Unsaved changes / Not saved yet).
  - Save keeps the pattern's values (pattern, grid, spacing, mark size, active, inactive, line gap, line length, frame trails, radius) for that style only, in this browser (everlab:hpMapStyle).
  - Choosing a style puts back what was saved for it.
  - On load, the showing style's saved values go on top of the panel's own.
  - Checked: Crosshair saved as Dots 6px, Frame as Plus 5px; switching brings each back; it survives a reload.
- **Frame: only inside lit** ("only active dots INSIDE the frame should be highlighted, not outside"): the marks inside the box are at the active opacity, those outside at the inactive; there's no soft edge past the box now.
- **Report items 2px apart** ("gap 2px").
- **+24px before the buttons** ("+24px padding left button gap"): the gap between the words and the Upload button or the switch goes from 14px to 38px.

- Frame trails now run across the whole map: from each side of the frame out to the map's edge, fading from the trail opacity to nothing as they near the edge (the frame rectangle itself stays solid white, with its corner squares).

- Trail opacity: the Frame style's trail slider is now called "Trail opacity". It sits right under Map style in the Past results Tweaks and shows only when Frame is picked. 0% hides the trails; 100% makes them as strong as the frame where they leave it, still fading to nothing at the map's edge. Saved with Save Frame.
- Added reports: 4px between items (was 2px).

- Documentation → Flows: a screen longer than the phone now scrolls in place. Use the wheel or trackpad over it, or drag it; the canvas takes over once the screen reaches its end. The wheel sticks to whichever it started on (the screen or the canvas) for the length of one gesture, so scrolling the canvas past a screen doesn't get caught by it. A thin bar at the screen's right shows while the pointer is over it or while it scrolls (4px wide, 5px in, at any zoom). Screens that fit are unchanged. "Reading the canvas" mentions it.
- Flows step headers: the next header now pushes the previous one up and out as it arrives, instead of stacking on top of it (each header sticks inside its own section). The title lines up with the first screen below it: sticky `left` already counted the canvas's 32px padding, so it was 32px too far right.

- Card screen: the card now sizes properly in the Documentation's Step 0 stills. The card's width comes from the screen's width, but a still drawn before its row was shown (Flows remembering another step, then Step 0 picked) read a width of 0. Its cards stayed at the 240px minimum instead of 320 on the phone, and Card back V1's five lines ran over "Member since". Now the card screen waits until it has a size, and re-places the card whenever its size changes (a ResizeObserver, released on destroy). Same in the app if it's ever opened inside something hidden; the live reveal is unchanged.

- Tweaks → Primary card ($299 purchased): a new **Documentation** row, under Open, with a "Health profile" button. It opens Documentation → Health profile card on Flows, showing the step the card's State is at (Step 2 → Step 2, Step 3.5 dropped off → Step 3, any All complete → All complete; a State with no step shows every step). The page's "Reading the canvas" mentions it.

## Panels push the viewport; 320px columns; card mask out with the card; new Steven photo

- Both docked panels now push the desktop full modals (the reveal, the profile, the report) instead of covering them. Flow sets the modal's left to `--flDockW`; Tweaks sets its right to `--tkDockW` and lets an open modal's width go (`width:auto`). Not at a forced XS/S: those phones stay centred by `--vwC` (applying it there had moved the phone screen off its device frame). The width release only applies to an open modal; a closed one collapsing made the Flow panel flicker.
- Both columns are 320px (`--flDockW`, `--tkDockW`, and the JS that reads the Tweaks dock width). The segmented switches inside the docked Tweaks are tighter (8px padding, 12px text) so three options fit.
- Desktop card screen to Steven's note: the card's dark mask (`.hpW2Bl`, a card-sized hole in a 200vmax box-shadow) used to stay behind as the card left, showing an outlined frame where the card had been. It now fades out over 260ms with the card.
- Steven's avatar is the new photo (832px jpg sent as a zip, decoded with ffmpeg, centre-cropped to 224px webp) in `assets/overview/avatar-steven.webp`. That updates the note and every other place the file is used.

## Concierge intro: slower bubbles, latest at full, centred; cards removed

- The bubbles come in about 1.5x slower: each step's wait is longer (450→700, 1200→1800, 1800→2700, 600→900, 1100→1650, held 2900→3200ms), and the entrance runs .7s (was .45s).
- Only the latest bubble is at full opacity; the ones before it sit at 50% (`.hpCcTh > .hpCcB:has(~ .hpCcB)`). The entrance animation now fills `backwards` only, so it no longer holds opacity at 1.
- The active bubble (or the Thinking indicator) is always centred vertically in the frame. On each new item the thread's `padding-bottom` is set so its middle meets the frame's middle, eased over .7s, with older bubbles rising above it. It resets when the loop starts again. Checked: an offset of 0px for each new bubble.
- Removed the three cards under the chat (Ask Eva anything, Reach your care team, Book in a few taps).

## Overview never on Step 1

- The Overview's Health profile card can no longer show Step 1. Whenever the card repaints, or the profile closes (`hpOn` removed), and the store is still at Step 1 with the profile not open, `step2()` sets it to Step 2 (`store.preset('one')`). This catches every way back to Step 1: a saved setup, the reveal's fresh profile after Steven's note, or the State tweak. Inside the profile and the onboarding, Step 1 still plays as before. Checked: the card shows "Book your consultation" after a load, after setting the State tweak to Step 1, and after going through the note and back to the Overview.

## From the Overview: Past results closes on Got it; no Flow panel

- The Overview's past results card opens Past results with `ov` (`_hp.past(0, true)`). There, Got it simply closes the modal; the HP `fwd()` for `res` calls `onClose` when `opts.ov && opts.solo === 'res'`. Opened from the Flow panel or Tweaks, Got it still leads on to the Concierge introduction.
- A page opened from the Overview (its Health profile card or its past results card) is a standalone page: no Flow panel, no Flow button, nothing docked (`window.__hpFromOv`, checked in `jny`). Opened from the Flow panel or Tweaks, the panel shows as before.

## Top bar "Page"; Past result card switch, under Primary; journey lights; card back member no.; Live version gap

- The top bar's "Version" label now reads "Page".
- The Past result card Tweaks group has an on/off switch in its header (`#stHpRecTgl`, saved through a hidden input `#stHpRecShow` = show/hide; `body.hpRecHide` hides `#dOver .hpRecOut`). A hidden select with On/Off became a second switch through the generic converter, hence the input. The group is placed right under the Primary card group (in `arrangeG`, before the First-time user groups).

## Concierge intro: H1 intro, cursor click, Thinking dot, photo frame, CTAs

- Opens on its own title, written the way the reveal's intro is: letter by letter from blur, with a warm touch. It reads "Every health question answered, / by Eva (AI) or a clinician", with AI in an outlined tag. It holds, lifts away, then the screen comes up into place and the loop starts.
- In the loop, after typing, a cursor comes in and clicks send. The field shrinks into an 8px dot with two ripples and "Thinking" under it (2s).
- Then an outlined frame comes in (24 radius, with the warm living-room photo dimmed inside it), framing the conversation.
- Every change to the thread glides as one motion (FLIP): bubbles in, Thinking out, the active bubble re-centred. Before, it snapped and then eased.
- The field follows the theme: grey a step off the page, its words and controls in the ink, the send lit in the ink.
- CTAs: Try concierge (opens the Concierge chat), with Go to overview as the secondary.
- Concierge field: a Beam border effect, like libraries.dev's border-beam (md, colorful, strength .7, dark), rebuilt in CSS since the prototype isn't React. A conic arc (orange, pink, violet, blue) rides the edge every 3.4s, with a blurred copy under it for the glow.
- Concierge loop: Thinking uses the Concierge chat page's own style. "Thinking…" under the dot and "Asking your care team…" in the thread, both muted, with a light passing through the words. It replaces the dot grid and label.
- The click is a white touch dot (34px, translucent, blurring what's under it). It replaces the arrow cursor.
- The field is 32px wider (32px in from the canvas's sides instead of 48px).
- The Beam light is more diffuse: a longer, fading tail, a soft 16px glow on the edge, and a wider 30px haze round it.
- Concierge loop: the frame and its photo are gone. Once the field shrinks into the Thinking dot, your video (assets/hp/concierge.webm, plus concierge.mp4 for Safari) fades in full-bleed behind the whole screen: header, conversation and buttons. It's 1152×648, no audio, about 1MB each, inlined by both builds (build.js and build-hp.js now take webm/mp4).
- A gradient of the page's ground runs down over the top of the video so the title reads, and a lighter one rises under the buttons. The member's bubble gets a light blur over the video.
- The video goes away when the loop resets or the screen is left.
- The WIP badge sits in the top bar, centred.
- Concierge Tweaks (on its screen): Layout is Title first (default) or Visual first, which puts the conversation above the title group. Video is Full (default) or Half: the top 50% of the screen, fading progressively into the page at its foot, with the page's ground under the buttons.
- Footer over the full video: one smooth fade from 96px above the buttons down. The old 40px fade above the footer, which met the new one with an edge, is gone.
- The field's Beam now follows the screen-recording reference, in warm orange tones: three soft lights rest on the edge at once and drift round it (7s). Their light spills inward as a soft glow inside the field, the line is lit faintly only near them, and a faint halo sits outside.
- Concierge loop: the field shrinks into the dot snappier (260ms, with a sharp ease) and the dot pops in. No ripple.
- Thinking follows the capture: the grid of dots turning over, "Thinking", then "· Looking at your records" muted. It shows centred under the dot and again in the thread before Eva's second reply, replacing the shimmer text.
